spec.description: PHASE 30: purpose-built around four questions the other five dashboards answer piecemeal -- what did the system learn (per-device thresholds), how did it tune itself (calibration history), what did it suppress (autonomous FP suppression funnel and releases, by source), and what couldn't it do (subsystem health/failures). Every panel here already exists elsewhere except the two new learned-threshold tables, the device-profile-correction breakdown, the persistence-escalation panel, and the four new health metrics -- this dashboard curates them into one narrative rather than duplicating logic. Prometheus-only.

spec.title: 🔍 What is this dashboard?
spec.description: Section header.

options.content: **Is the system actually getting smarter, and can I trust what it does while I'm not watching?** This dashboard answers that in four parts, top to bottom: **what it learned** (per-device thresholds it has calibrated for itself), **how it tuned** (the calibration history behind those numbers -- applied vs refused, not just applied), **what it suppressed** (autonomous false-positive suppression, broken down by stage and by source -- autonomous vs LLM-validated vs a human tap), and **what it couldn't do** (every subsystem's live health, so a quiet dashboard elsewhere can be told apart from a genuinely healthy one). Most panels here are curated copies of panels that already exist on the Autonomous Behavior and System Health dashboards -- this view exists to answer the four questions directly, not to replace those.

spec.title: 📚 What It Learned — Per-Device Thresholds
spec.description: Section header.

options.content: Devices that have earned their own calibrated threshold, distinct from the global config.yaml default -- a device not listed in a given table below still uses that global value. Four independent learned thresholds now exist: the general FP-suppress threshold, and three detector-specific ones (ARP-sweep unique-targets, connection-abuse unique-IP, long-connection duration) added as false-positive patterns specific to each detector were found.

spec.title: ⚙️ Suppress Threshold — Effective (Per-Device)
spec.description: home_ids_autotune_device_threshold_effective -- devices with >=3 pooled corrections of their own evidence get their own calibrated fp_combined_suppress_threshold.

spec.title: ⚙️ ARP-Sweep Threshold — Effective (Per-Device)
spec.description: home_ids_autotune_arp_sweep_threshold_effective -- PHASE 30 gap fix, had sibling calibration/evidence panels but was never itself plotted anywhere until this session.

spec.title: ⚙️ Connection-Abuse Unique-IP Threshold — Effective (Per-Device)
spec.description: PHASE 30 (new this session): home_ids_autotune_conn_abuse_threshold_effective -- threat_signals.py's zeek_conn_abuse check (s0_rej_unique > threshold) per device.

spec.title: ⚙️ Long-Connection Duration Threshold — Effective (Per-Device)
spec.description: PHASE 30 (new this session): home_ids_autotune_long_conn_threshold_effective -- threat_signals.py's zeek_long_conn check (max_duration > threshold) per device.

spec.title: ⚙️ Global Suppress Threshold — Effective vs Baseline
spec.description: The single most direct 'is the system healing itself' chart: the live effective fp_combined_suppress_threshold against your hand-set config.yaml baseline. Effective should trend at or below baseline over time, never above.

spec.title: ⚙️ How It Tuned — Calibration History
spec.description: Section header.

options.content: Refusals are as informative as applications -- proof the system isn't blindly loosening just because it can. Two calibration mechanisms exist: a weekly bidirectional pass (train_fp_classifier.py, covers the suppress and ARP-sweep thresholds) and immediate reactive corrections (fp_engine.py, covers all four thresholds whenever a specific alert is corrected -- the bottom table breaks these down by threshold key and by who/what made the correction).

spec.title: ⚙️ Global Calibration Pass Outcomes (Cumulative)
spec.description: applied / refused_ambiguous / insufficient_samples / no_change_needed, across both scope=global and scope=device.

spec.title: ⚙️ ARP-Sweep Calibration Outcomes (Cumulative)
spec.description: Same shape as the global calibration panel, for the separate bidirectional ARP-sweep-threshold rule (train_fp_classifier.py's calibrate_arp_sweep_threshold()).

spec.title: ⚙️ Evidence Samples Pooled (Global)
spec.description: How close the global pass is to its next calibration decision: corrected = confirmed FPs pooled since the last write, uncorrected = never-corrected UNCERTAIN alerts in the same window.

spec.title: ⚙️ ARP-Sweep Evidence Pool (corrected vs confirmed)
spec.description: Per-device CONNECTION_ABUSE correction/confirmation counts feeding the ARP-sweep calibration pass.

spec.title: ⚙️ Device-Profile Corrections by Threshold Key & Source
spec.description: PHASE 30 (new this session): home_ids_autotune_device_profile_correction_total -- cumulative reactive/calibration corrections applied to a device's learned-threshold profile, by which threshold key was touched and who/what made the correction (operator = a Telegram 'Mark False Positive' tap, llm_validated = Ollama's autonomous validation pass, or a train_fp_classifier.py calibration tag). set_by reflects the MOST RECENT correction for that device+key, not a full history across every source ever used.

spec.title: 🚫 What It Suppressed
spec.description: Section header.

options.content: The full suppression funnel (evaluated -> hard-stopped -> suppressed), then the by-source breakdown of every autonomous self-healing action: domains immunized, sensitivity adjustments, Pi-hole unblocks, and router-isolation releases. The goal of this whole self-calibration system is for 'autonomous' and 'llm_validated' to dominate 'operator' over time -- a human shouldn't need to keep pace with every alert for the system to keep healing itself.

spec.title: 🧪 CL-AFPE 3-Stage Funnel (Evaluated → Hard-Stopped → Suppressed)
spec.description: How many alerts CL-AFPE evaluated, how many were confirmed threats (hard-stop bypass, never eligible for suppression), and how many were actually suppressed as false positives.

spec.title: 🛡️ Domains Immunized by Source
spec.description: fp_engine_domains_immunized_total split by source (autonomous / operator / llm_validated).

spec.title: 🛡️ Sensitivity Adjustments by Source
spec.description: fp_engine_sigma_shifts_total split by source (autonomous / operator / llm_validated).

spec.title: 🔓 Pi-hole Unblocks by Reason
spec.description: 'immunized' = an autonomous or operator correction released a block that was no longer warranted. 'manual' = an explicit operator release. The release-side counterpart to the block-side count on the Main Overview dashboard.

spec.title: 🔓 Router Isolation Releases by Reason
spec.description: home_ids_ips_router_releases_total split by reason (immunized / manual) -- the release-side counterpart to router isolation on the Main Overview dashboard.

spec.title: 🩺 What It Couldn't Do — Subsystem Health
spec.description: Section header.

options.content: Every subsystem's live health in one place, plus one honesty signal: how often an alert's severity grew from a signal simply persisting rather than genuine new corroboration. A quiet 'What It Learned'/'How It Tuned' section above can mean either a genuinely calm network, or a subsystem below silently failing to feed it evidence -- this section is what tells the two apart.

spec.title: Zeek Network Monitor
spec.description: home_ids_zeek_status -- reference copy of the Overview dashboard's identical panel.

spec.title: Pi-hole IPS
spec.description: home_ids_ips_pihole_status -- reference copy of the Overview dashboard's identical panel.

spec.title: 🦈 Suricata Binary Health (Boot-Time)
spec.description: PHASE 30: home_ids_suricata_binary_health -- the one-shot --build-info smoke test result from main.py's boot sequence. No data = reactive_capture_suricata_enabled is false. See the next panel for the live scan success rate.

spec.title: 🦈 Suricata Live Scan Health
spec.description: PHASE 30: home_ids_suricata_scan_total's live success/error ratio over the last 30m -- the actual batch-scan invocations reactive-capture bursts dispatch.

spec.title: 🌐 Pi-hole Gravity-List API Health
spec.description: PHASE 30: time since the last successful home_ids_pihole_gravity_last_success_timestamp -- the live CDN/telemetry-recognition lookup against your own Pi-hole's gravity list.

spec.title: 📅 Scheduled-Job Health
spec.description: Time since each scheduled job's last successful completion, and how long that run took. Expected staleness: ollama_soc ~4h, retro_hunter/top_domains_report/train_fp_classifier ~24h.

spec.title: Reactive-Capture Errors by Stage (Cumulative Rate)
spec.description: Where in the pipeline a reactive-capture burst failed: capture, conversion, zeek_reprocess, suricata_scan, or dns_evasion_audit. Should trend toward zero.

spec.title: 🧭 Persistence-Escalated Alerts by Signature
spec.description: PHASE 30 (new this session): home_ids_persistence_escalation_total -- alerts whose confidence/state was escalated purely because the SAME uncorroborated signal kept recurring, not because of new independent evidence. Deliberately capped below every genuinely-corroborated HIGH and excluded from authorizing IPS containment on its own -- a form of 'what it couldn't do' (couldn't get independent corroboration, escalated on persistence alone instead).
